Description
Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route National Historic Trail - driving route and related sites.
Purpose
This 680-mile-long trail follows the paths taken by George Washington's Continental Army and Jean-Baptiste de Rochambeau's Expédition Particulière during their 1781 march from Newport, Rhode Island, to Yorktown, Virginia. France's support in America's struggle for independence was vital to victory at Yorktown. The trail commemorates that victory and the lasting Franco-American friendship. These data were created to allow visitors to drive an approximate representation of those paths and visit related sites.
